independent.summary: A go.mod's Service title is the last path segment with no handling of Go's semantic import versioning: `module github.com/acme/ledger-feed/v2` (the normal spelling for any Go module at major version ≥ 2, and the very form the fixture's own dependencies use — `pgx/v5`, `go-redis/v9`) is titled "v2". Worse, titles are the dedup key: importing two different v2+ Go modules into one workspace makes the second an `exact-normalized-title` update of the first, merging two unrelated services into one entity. Only the module itself is affected — dependencies keep their full path as the title — and the unit/HTTP fixtures use a v1 path, so no test covers it.

The hand-written TOML `readValue` recurses per nested array/inline table with no depth bound, so a 60,000-character file such as `[package]\nname="x"\nx = [[[[[…` (accepted by `detectFamily` as TOML) overflows the stack. The resulting RangeError is not a ManifestParseError, so the route's catch falls through to `next(err)` and the caller gets a 500 instead of the 400-with-a-line the producer promises for an unreadable file.

PEP 621 build requirements (`[build-system].requires`) are dropped with no drop reason and are not added to `counts.dropped`, while the exactly analogous Cargo `[build-dependencies]` table is reported and counted. The producer's own rule is "dropped with a REASON rather than silently, so a reviewer who expected to see `jest` can find out where it went"; a reviewer importing the suite's own pyproject fixture gets three drop reasons and no mention of `hatchling` at all.

triageGrades.reason: No authentication or authorization logic is added or changed — the new route inherits the existing `requireWriteRole` mount and `resolveWorkspace`; the cited evidence is just the producer file's header comment.

Right call despite the arbitrary line reference: the change adds a new credential-bearing ingestion path (documented as redacted before storage) plus fixtures containing fake tokens and tests asserting they never reach the draft or the database.
No billing, quota or allowance logic is modified — the producer is deterministic, makes no model call, and the quota test only asserts the allowance is left untouched.
The change only creates draft rows; it deletes nothing, runs no migration, and the enum addition to `Draft.source.producer` is purely additive.
No outbound calls are added — reading a Git remote or any provider API is explicitly out of scope, and parsing is entirely local.
No CI, deploy, packaging or infrastructure configuration is touched; the only non-code changes are docs and the decision log.

summary: The local review found nothing at all in a 1,000-line hand-written parser — missing the go.mod `/vN` titling bug, the unbounded TOML recursion that turns a malformed file into a 500, and an asymmetric silent drop — and its only two positive triage calls were a wrong "auth: touched" and a right "secrets: touched" backed by a meaningless line reference.
